# Candidate literature conformance fixtures

All identities, text, numerical values and sources here are fictional. The binary
file contains only an inert PDF-like header; no PDF parser or native job is used.
No file here is an authenticated acquisition/extraction receipt.

`conformance.json` contains one request/candidate pair per operation. Providers
use the same envelope regardless of ranking implementation. The test module
validates these pairs and supplies refusal siblings for budgets, snapshots,
locations, source mutation, missing groups and authority promotion.

`source.txt` supports exact original-text and comparison-literal checks.
`pdf-evidence.json`, `original.bin` and `extraction.json` exercise page-text
coordinates and original/extraction hashes using supplied inert records. Actual
broker serving must additionally authenticate the producing receipt and source
binding with the existing extraction consumer.

`legacy-atlas.json` and `legacy-{show,find,limit,miss}.json` are fixed golden
fixtures for the existing knowledge API with no retrieval index. Expected bytes
were constructed independently from the legacy envelope specification, including
its sorted, indented JSON with a trailing newline and SHA256 fields. They are
not regenerated by the tests. The new contract uses compact canonical JSON for
its byte budgets; it does not change that older format.

The normative contract is the packaged retrieval schema plus
`validate_request`, `validate_candidates`, `validate_evidence` and
`verify_excerpt` in `ravel.workflow.literature_provider`. All authority booleans
remain false. Null measurement units/conditions mean unsourced. Pagination uses
`selector_digest` as well as index/policy identity and provider-validated tokens.

A structural conformance pass establishes neither source-policy enforcement
before ranking nor authenticated serving, model quality, corpus completeness or
scientific validity. Provider-specific tests must prove filtering before any
ranking/statistics/expansion, cursor token authentication and resource stopping.
The broker separately enforces current policy, receipts and source custody.
